Ben Evans, Lenny, Mitchell Hashimoto, One Useful Thing, Stratechery: no new items in window or not AI-relevant; The Atlantic Technology: nothing new since Nov 19.
HN: ≥200-point AI items in last 48h taken; many HN items off-topic.

candidates.summary: amasad says a high school student is recompiling GTA6 to run on PC and coordinating tasks across agent swarms using GitHub issues; he asks if this is a new model for open source.

kloss_xyz describes a 'skill audit': spawn 2 Cursor cloud agents to run read-only audits with Gemini 4 Neon and Fable 5.2 on xhigh effort, then apply only edits the models agree on, highest confidence first.
facts: All 3 agreed on edits to 22 of his 104 skills (his figure: 21% of his stack).
Advice: run this every time a new model drops.

candidates.summary: MengTo says GPT 6.2 Astra recreated a desk scene in three.js with every desk object interactive, and a sunset toggle on a Liquid Glass UI warms the room; he open-sourced 3 skills.
facts: Skills: liquid glass, press shaders, 3D room (GitHub MengTo/Skills).

candidates.summary: kunchenguid notes that the Riemann hypothesis was reportedly solved by Anthropic and that OpenAI has said nothing, and asks when labs can set aside ego and celebrate achievements together.
The Verge reports Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims to have proved the Riemann hypothesis with help from Claude.
facts: The solution has not been independently verified.
Anthropic has not commented or involved itself in the announcement, per The Verge.

The Verge podcast (Nov 21): 'Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?' says Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday.
HN also shows 'Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory' (479 points).

candidates.summary: arXiv paper 'Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights' (2611.21885) discussed on HN.
MIT Technology Review covers METR's updated report on AI task performance.
facts: Frontier models are doubling performance on verifiable tasks every four months, per the article summary.
Models still fall short of humans on judgment, e.g. designing new AI evaluations or scoring philosophical arguments.

facts: Dumpleton has published a detailed account of the project as he builds it, all in the last three weeks.
